mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month (measured by the change in FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.1% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05 over 5-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5% in current and prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% for two consecutive months (over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., positive returns < 60% of the time) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) signals potential overheating and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, INDPRO rises fail to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., negative returns < 60% of the time) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month indicates strengthening economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises fail to predict positive returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., positive returns < 60% of the time) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% (over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases fail to predict positive returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., positive returns < 60% of the time) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals potential overbuilding and impending correction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, HOUST rises fail to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., negative returns < 60% of the time) over 3-year rolling windows.
